boundary_rationale: The front seam of this span falls at the acrostic letter change from mem (Lam.3.39) to nun (Lam.3.40), where the voice also shifts from the singular reflection of Lam.3.39 to the plural cohortative onset of Lam.3.40; the nun and samekh-letter triplets (3:40-42, 3:43-45) open a first-person-plural confession, spliced at byte tier from its cohortative onset as נַחְפְּשָׂ֤ה דְרָכֵ֨ינוּ֙ וְֽנַחְקֹ֔רָה וְנָשׁ֖וּבָה עַד יְהוָֽה (oshb:Lam.3.40, byte tier), rendered by the WEB witness “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to Yahweh.” (web:Lam.3.40); whether this turn belongs with the reflection ending at Lam.3.39 or with the confession beginning at Lam.3.40 is held rather than decided. The plural voice continues, spliced at byte tier as נַ֤חְנוּ פָשַׁ֨עְנוּ֙ וּמָרִ֔ינוּ אַתָּ֖ה לֹ֥א סָלָֽחְתָּ (oshb:Lam.3.42, byte tier; WEB “We have transgressed and have rebelled. Ending the span at Lam.3.47 cuts inside the pe triplet one verse short of its close at Lam.3.48; the SAMEKH mark there corroborates, at tier-3 single-witness weight, mild continuity across the cut, weighed against and outweighed by the tier-1 pronoun-shift warrant that follows. The back seam's tier-1 signal is the pronoun shift itself: Lam.3.48 turns the plural back to a singular first person on עֵינִ֔י (oshb:Lam.3.48, byte tier; “my eye”), a byte-observable person shift this span treats as the stronger signal over the triplet's own formal boundary.

boundary_rationale: The qof and resh triplets (3:55-57, 3:58-60) turn the geber's first-person report into direct second-person address to YHWH, spliced at byte tier from its opening invocation as קָרָ֤אתִי שִׁמְךָ֙ יְהוָ֔ה מִבּ֖וֹר תַּחְתִּיּֽוֹת (oshb:Lam.3.55, byte tier), matched by the WEB witness “I called on your name, Yahweh, out of the lowest dungeon.” (web:Lam.3.55). The qof triplet closes with reported reassurance at Lam.3.57, its nested divine reply spliced at byte tier as אַל תִּירָֽא (oshb:Lam.3.57, byte tier), rendered by the WEB witness “Don’t be afraid.” (web:Lam.3.57), and the resh triplet opens under the Adonai title, spliced at byte tier as רַ֧בְתָּ אֲדֹנָ֛י רִיבֵ֥י נַפְשִׁ֖י גָּאַ֥לְתָּ חַיָּֽי (oshb:Lam.3.58, byte tier; WEB “Lord, you have pleaded the causes of my soul. The span's back seam, at Lam.3.60/Lam.3.61, rests on the acrostic letter change from resh to shin, and no accompanying voice, addressee or topic shift falls at either verse; the report of the enemies' plotting against the speaker continues in content and address across that seam, disclosed here as the continuity this span's own confidence takes into account.

boundary_rationale: The span's front seam, at Lam.3.60/Lam.3.61, rests on the acrostic letter change from resh to shin, and no accompanying voice, addressee or topic shift falls at either verse; the direct address to YHWH about the enemies' hostility continues across that seam without a content break, disclosed here as part of this span's own confidence assessment. The shin and tav triplets (3:61-63, 3:64-66) close the whole triple acrostic, reporting the enemies' plotting under direct address to YHWH through 3:61-3:63, the shin triplet's one true imperative anchored at הַבִּ֔יטָה (oshb:Lam.3.63, byte tier) amid its closing report clauses, before turning, in the tav triplet, to three verse-initial second-masculine-singular prefix-conjugation verbs of prospective retribution against them, each verse-initial in the same construction (sweep: 3 verses): תָּשִׁ֨יב לָהֶ֥ם גְּמ֛וּל יְהוָ֖ה כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Lam.3.64, byte tier), תִּתֵּ֤ן לָהֶם֙ מְגִנַּת לֵ֔ב תַּאֲלָֽתְךָ֖ לָהֶֽם (oshb:Lam.3.65, byte tier) and תִּרְדֹּ֤ף בְּאַף֙ וְתַשְׁמִידֵ֔ם מִתַּ֖חַת שְׁמֵ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Lam.3.66, byte tier); the WEB witness renders the opening verb “You will pay them back, Yahweh, according to the work of their hands.” (web:Lam.3.64) and the closing verb, at the poem's own final verse, “You will pursue them in anger, and destroy them from under the heavens of Yahweh.” (web:Lam.3.66). This closing shift from report to prospective retribution is the disclosed reason the span is not extended further back into the qof/resh material; it is an operative-category deviation from a plain unit_type label, disclosed here rather than left silent.

boundary_rationale: The stanza sequence opens the chapter with אֵיכָה֙ יוּעַ֣ם זָהָ֔ב (oshb:Lam.4.1, byte tier), rendered by the WEB witness “How the gold has become dim!” (web:Lam.4.1); its opening word אֵיכָה֙ also opens the poems at Lam.1.1 and Lam.2.1 (accent_stripped tier; sweep: 4 hits book-wide, verse-initial in three of them). Two verses of tarnished-treasure imagery, the gold and the sons of Zion counted as pitchers, give way to the narrator's indictment that “the daughter of my people has become cruel” (web:Lam.4.3), her cruelty toward her young set against nursing jackals — the verse's own doubled ketiv/qere pair disclosed here: unpointed ketiv תנין against pointed qere תַּנִּים֙ for the jackals themselves, and unpointed ketiv כי ענים against pointed qere כַּיְעֵנִ֖ים for the ostrich comparison (oshb:Lam.4.3, both notes single-witness apparatus), the plural nursing-jackals wording here following the qere rather than the singular ketiv — then pressed further by the Sodom comparison that closes the group: “the iniquity of the daughter of my people is greater than the sin of Sodom” (web:Lam.4.6). The stanzas run aleph, bet, gimel, dalet, he and vav, positions one through six of the reversed pe-before-ayin sequence that governs this chapter. The span's back seam, at Lam.4.6/Lam.4.7, turns on the shift from the Sodom-comparison indictment to the nobles' description beginning at Lam.4.7, weighed against the bat-ami phrase's own recurrence at Lam.4.10, disclosed in device_notes as a pull toward continuity across this seam.

The span's front seam, at Lam.4.6/Lam.4.7, is weighed against the bat-ami phrase's own recurrence across Lam.4.6 and Lam.4.10, disclosed in device_notes as a device straddling this boundary rather than merely framing it.
